answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent's voting weight to a stake it cannot withdraw quickly. A fake identity costs nothing to spawn, but locked collateral is hard to forge, so creating a thousand puppet agents becomes expensive. Peers can also watch history over time: an agent that only ever attests for its own kin gets its weight cut. The stake works like an anchor that keeps a node from drifting into the jetty of fake consensus.
